Subjective:
- Current issues:
  - Diarrhea x ~3 days; 4–5 bowel movements/day; consistency varies from watery to loose depending on time of day.
  - Mild abdominal pain.
  - One episode of vomiting.
  - Possible mild fever (“maybe a little bit”).
  - Decreased appetite but able to maintain oral fluid intake.
  - Denies blood or mucus in stool.
  - No recent travel; no unusual foods or suspected foodborne exposure; has not taken any treatments yet.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma (patient uncertain if still active; “had asthma… guess I still have it”).
- Family history:
  - Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62.
- Medications:
  - Lexapro — dose/route/frequency not documented. (Note: stated in response to “which inhaler,” conflict noted.)
  - Reports using an inhaler — name not confirmed; conflict noted.
  - No over-the-counter medications taken for current symptoms.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- General (telemedicine): Clinician notes patient appears not dehydrated on video.
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Physical exam: Not performed (telemedicine).
- Investigations: None performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhea:
   - Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Stool sample if diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Oral hydration; consider oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte).
     - Soft diet: crackers, toast, jam; avoid dairy, meat, eggs, and fish during acute phase.
     - Yogurt permitted for probiotics.
     - Progress to boiled/mashed vegetables; reintroduce meat/eggs/fish after 48 hours without diarrhea.
   - Safety-net/follow-up:
     - Seek care if frequency increases to ~6–8+ times/day or signs of dehydration develop.
     - Return/seek care if symptoms persist >1 week, blood in stool, or overall worsening.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure), weight.
  - Detailed hydration assessment (urine output, orthostasis).
  - Full medication list with doses/routes/frequencies; specific inhaler names.
  - Surgical history.
  - Broader social history (tobacco, alcohol, substance use, occupation).
  - Full review of systems for red flags (severe abdominal pain, recent antibiotics, sick contacts).
- Internal conflicts:
  - Inhaler use: patient answered “Yes” to inhalers but then named “Lexapro” when asked which inhaler — conflict noted.
  - Asthma status: “had asthma” vs “still have it” — conflict noted.
  - Dehydration/urgent threshold stated as “>8 times/day” in one instance and “~6–8 times/day” in another — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Occasional unclear audio (e.g., patient statement “Mostly it’s been dry and red” context unclear; medication name heard as “Laxepro” vs “Lexapro”).
